name: Alpbach
kurzbeschreibung: The most beautiful village in Austria – flower-adorned balcony houses and the Alpbacher mountain landscape.
beschreibung:
Overview

Alpbach is nestled at an elevation of 975 meters in the scenic Alpbachtal valley within Tyrol's Kufstein district, surrounded by the grassy ridges and limestone peaks of the Kitzbühel Alps. Covering more than 70 square kilometers, the municipality spans from the valley entrance up to the Großer Galtenberg at 2,424 meters, the highest peak in the district. Approximately 2,500 residents live in the main village and the upper valley hamlet of Inneralpbach. Alpbach holds legendary status: voted 'Austria's Most Beautiful Village' in 1983 and awarded the title of 'Most Beautiful Floral Village in Europe' in 1993, its immaculate aesthetic is protected by a strict 1953 municipal building code mandating that all structures above ground floor must be built entirely in traditional Tyrolean timber architecture.

History

Settlement in the valley dates to before the turn of the first millennium, with the earliest documented record appearing around 1240. In the 15th and 16th centuries, rich copper and silver mining in the Luegergraben and Gratlspitz brought prosperity. The renowned Fugger merchant dynasty from Augsburg oversaw the mining operations, using the historic Böglerhof inn as their mining court. In August 1945, right after World War II, Otto Molden and Simon Moser founded the international interdisciplinary seminar that evolved into the European Forum Alpbach (EFA). Dubbed the 'Village of Thinkers', Alpbach hosts over 4,000 global leaders, Nobel laureates, and scholars each summer. Physicist and Nobel laureate Erwin Schrödinger made Alpbach his spiritual retreat; his grave in the Saint Oswald churchyard features his wave equation.

Getting There

By rail, travelers take express trains to the transport hubs of Jenbach or Wörgl and switch to regional services to Brixlegg station. From the station square in Brixlegg, VVT regional bus line 620 delivers passengers directly into central Alpbach and Inneralpbach in about 15 to 20 minutes; bus transit is free for arriving guests with an accommodation voucher. By car, take the Inntal Motorway A12 to exit 32 Kramsach/Alpbachtal and follow the L5 Alpbachtal road via Reith uphill for about ten kilometers. Innsbruck Airport is approximately 57 kilometers away, while Munich Airport lies around 145 kilometers to the north.

Tips

In winter, the acclaimed Ski Juwel Alpbachtal Wildschönau ski area boasts 114 kilometers of slopes and 45 lifts, including the modern Wiedersbergerhorn gondola. Summer hiking is world-class: ascending the Großer Galtenberg (2,424 m) rewards hikers with alpine vistas of the Zillertal Alps, while the rocky Gratlspitze (1,899 m) is famous for sunrise hikes. Families enjoy the Lauserland nature play park and the year-round 'Lauser-Sauser' alpine coaster at the Wiedersbergerhorn mountain station. In Inneralpbach, the Vorder-Unterberg Farmhouse Museum—a preserved homestead from 1638—showcases historical mountain farming. Other essential sights include the green-certified Congress Centrum Alpbach and Erwin Schrödinger's commemorative grave at Saint Oswald's church.
